h1: Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel — Spacious, Clean Rooms With Free Parking in the City, Near the Station
intro: If you want a city-centre stay in Phitsanulok with spacious, clean rooms, free parking and a wallet-friendly price, Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel (Morage Hotel) is the name guests bring up for its 30 m² rooms that feel bigger than the price suggests · This midrange 3-star, 44-room hotel opened in 2015 and was renovated in 2021, set in Nai Mueang about 1.7 km from Phitsanulok Railway Station · What reviewers consistently praise is the spacious, clean rooms, friendly staff, free breakfast and free parking · Rooms from approx ฿700/night

body.html: Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel, known to Thais as Morage Hotel, opened in 2015 and was renovated in 2021, set in Nai Mueang, Mueang Phitsanulok — a central location that sits about 1.7 km from Phitsanulok Railway Station and makes getting around the city easy · It's a midrange 44-room hotel whose main draw is its 30 m² rooms, more spacious than many city hotels at the same price · Guests here for work, arriving by train, or stopping over before continuing to Sukhothai or Khao Kho tend to pick it for a roomy stay with free parking at good value.

The 30 m² rooms are decorated in warm tones with air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, free Wi-Fi and an in-room seating area · The thing reviewers say most often is that the rooms are spacious, clean and quiet · There are Superior and Deluxe rooms with a queen or twin beds, all the same 30 m² size · Worth knowing: some reviews mention weak shower water pressure and the occasional bathroom-cleanliness issue still to be ironed out — flag it at the front desk as soon as you check in if anything isn't right.
"The room was really spacious for the price, clean, comfortable bed, helpful staff, and free breakfast plus free parking too. Great value at this rate."

Service is another strong point · Staff are praised for being friendly and helpful, the front desk runs 24 hours, and there is a shared lounge and a small garden · The hotel has free private parking, which is very convenient for self-drivers, plus an in-house restaurant open in the evening · Breakfast is a free Thai–international buffet — most reviews say it's appropriate for the price and nicely presented, even if the spread isn't as large as a big hotel's — a solid way to start the day before heading out.

The location works well for travellers arriving by train or driving themselves · It's about 1.7 km from Phitsanulok Railway Station, just a few minutes' drive · From the hotel it's roughly a 10-minute drive to the Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) area to pay respects to Phra Phuttha Chinnarat and stroll along the Nan River · Central Plaza Phitsanulok and the bus terminal are short drives away too · The overall score sits around 8.8 from 135 Trip.com reviews — solid, with a review base large enough to trust for a hotel at this level.

To be honest, Moraj is a city hotel that isn't within walking distance of Wat Yai and has no river view or swimming pool · It isn't right in the riverside old-town district, so you'll drive or ride in about 10 minutes · If you want a room overlooking the Nan River or a riverside boutique feel, Dragon River Avenue or Grand Riverside may suit better · But if you want a spacious 30 m² room that's clean, with free parking, free breakfast and near the station at an easy price — Moraj offers room-space value that's hard to find in this city.

A tip from following reviews here: if you're driving, the free on-site parking is a real advantage in a city where parking is scarce · If you arrive by train, the 1.7 km from the station is a quick ride and the hotel can help arrange transport · And if you run into weak water pressure or a bathroom-cleanliness issue, flag it at the front desk straight away — staff here are praised for being helpful and usually sort it out.

honestSummary: Moraj is a strong pick in Phitsanulok for anyone who wants a spacious 30 m² room that's clean, with free parking, free breakfast, central and near the railway station at an easy price · The generous room space is a genuine strength — but accept that the hotel isn't within walking distance of Wat Yai (about a 10-minute drive to the old town), some reviews mention weak shower pressure, and there's no pool or river view.
honestChecks: If you want a room overlooking the Nan River or a riverside boutique feel — this is a city hotel with no water view → try Dragon River Avenue or Grand Riverside in the same city instead

If you want to walk to Wat Yai to pay respects to Phra Phuttha Chinnarat — the hotel is about a 10-minute drive from the old town → choose a stay in the Wat Yai area like Holatel or Wangchan Riverview if walking matters
If you're particular about water pressure and bathroom cleanliness — some reviews note issues still to be ironed out → flag it at the front desk on check-in and choose a free-cancellation rate

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel

faq.q: Where is Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel · is it near the railway station?
faq.a: It's at 59/70 Sridhammatraipitak Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Phitsanulok · It's about 1.7 km from Phitsanulok Railway Station, just a few minutes' drive · From the hotel it's roughly a 10-minute drive to the Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) area and the Nan River · Central Plaza Phitsanulok and the bus terminal are short drives away too, and the airport about 12 minutes.

faq.q: How much does Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel cost · what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx ฿700/night for a Superior with a queen bed · Every room is 30 m²; there are Superior and Deluxe rooms with a queen or twin beds, with Deluxe around ฿850–900 · Prices vary by date and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for anyone who wants a spacious 30 m² room that's clean, with free parking, free breakfast, central and near the railway station at an easy price · The generous room space is the standout · Ideal for self-drivers, business travellers, train arrivals, or those stopping in Phitsanulok before Sukhothai or Khao Kho who value a roomy stay over a river view or walking to the temple.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Moraj really spacious and clean?
faq.a: Every room is 30 m² and the spaciousness and cleanliness of the rooms are what reviewers praise most · Rooms have warm tones and an in-room seating area, and the hotel was renovated in 2021 · Worth knowing: some reviews mention weak shower water pressure and the occasional bathroom-cleanliness issue still to be ironed out — flag it at the front desk as soon as you check in if anything isn't right.

Yes — there is free private parking, which is very convenient in a city where parking is scarce · Breakfast is a free Thai–international buffet; most reviews say it's appropriate for the price and nicely presented, even if the spread isn't as large as a big hotel's · There's also an in-house restaurant in the evening, a shared lounge, a small garden and a 24-hour front desk.

faq.q: How many rooms does Moraj Phitsanulok Hotel have · what are the review scores like?
faq.a: The hotel has 44 rooms, opened in 2015 and renovated in 2021 · The overall score is around 8.8 from 135 Trip.com reviews — solid, with a review base large enough to trust for a hotel at this level · Book ahead on long weekends and festivals, and choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm.
